methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective cohort of children (<=15 years) with acute leukemia treated 2004-2024, comparing patients with abdominal pain who did versus did not meet modified pediatric Atlanta/INSPPIRE criteria for acute pancreatitis, and estimating AP prevalence among 618 leukemia patients (Methods; Methods 2.1). The design is appropriate for prevalence and risk-factor exploration, but AP case ascertainment is restricted to those presenting with abdominal pain and may miss asymptomatic/mild cases, and the retrospective record review limits control of confounding. The statistical plan uses appropriate univariable and multivariable logistic regression with an explicit variable-selection threshold and reports ORs with 95% CIs (Methods 2.3), supporting the risk-factor analysis quality.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual observational cohort assessing prevalence and predictors of a clinically important chemotherapy complication, which maps to Oxford LoE 2b. The outcomes are directly relevant to pediatric oncology care, including associations with mortality and identification of risk factors related to protocol intensity and cumulative L-asparaginase exposure (Abstract; Results 3.4). The findings could inform monitoring and dosing practices, though they are not tested in an interventional framework.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is appropriate for this retrospective cohort, and the manuscript specifies setting and timeframe, inclusion logic, diagnostic criteria for AP, chemotherapy protocol eras, and the analytic approach (Methods 2.1-2.3). The report would be stronger with a clearer accounting of missing laboratory/imaging data and a more explicit patient-flow description from 618 leukemia patients to the 70 abdominal-pain subgroup and 17 AP cases (Abstract; Methods/Results). Data and code are not shared in the normalized manuscript; analyses are described as run in R without an accessible dataset or scripts.

novelty_literature.justification: The study provides a long time-horizon single-center estimate of AP prevalence in childhood leukemia and identifies protocol intensity and a cumulative L-asparaginase dose cutoff (>=55,200 IU/m2) as risk factors (Abstract; Results 3.4). While clinically useful locally, the work is primarily confirmatory of known asparaginase-associated pancreatitis risk patterns and does not introduce a new mechanism or validated predictive model.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with a structured abstract that states cohort size, AP prevalence, and the main risk factors (Abstract). Methods define AP diagnostic criteria and chemotherapy protocol categories and describe the regression approach in a transparent way (Methods 2.1-2.3). Results are organized by patient characteristics, clinical profiles, management, and risk factors, making the narrative easy to follow (Results 3.1-3.4).

key_strengths: Clinically relevant cohort over two decades with explicit pediatric AP diagnostic criteria and chemotherapy protocol stratification (Methods 2.1-2.2).
Appropriate multivariable logistic regression approach for risk-factor assessment, with ORs and 95% CIs (Methods 2.3).
Actionable exposure signal around higher-risk protocols and cumulative L-asparaginase dosing associated with AP risk (Abstract; Results 3.4).
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center design with case ascertainment limited to children presenting with abdominal pain may bias prevalence and risk estimates (Methods).
Limited detail on missingness and patient flow from the full leukemia population to analyzed subgroups reduces transparency (Abstract/Methods/Results).
No data/code availability statement is present, limiting reproducibility and external validation.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a useful retrospective toxicity epidemiology study with reasonable statistical methods, but it is limited by ascertainment and single-center retrospective design and would need stronger reporting and robustness checks for tier-3 acceptance.
